title: Kafka Consumer Group Rebalance Lag & Static Membership
subtitle: Tuning Cooperative Sticky Assignors, Heartbeat Threads and max.poll.interval.ms
problem_statement: A telemetry processing pipeline consumes from 64 Kafka partitions using 16 worker pods. During a garbage collection pause of 35 seconds or slow database batch inserts, the consumer exceeds max.poll.interval.ms. The Kafka group coordinator considers the consumer dead and triggers an eager Stop-The-World rebalance, halting all 16 workers and compounding consumer lag exponentially.

faded_bug.description: Synchronous record-by-record processing inside poll loop risks exceeding max.poll.interval.ms and triggering consumer rebalance.

invariants.description: Consumer lag must remain bounded without triggering stop-the-world eager rebalances.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the difference between heartbeat thread (`session.timeout.ms`) and the polling thread (`max.poll.interval.ms`) in Kafka Consumer architecture.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: During rolling deployments in Kubernetes, 16 pods are restarted one by one. With default Eager Assignor, how many rebalances occur and what is the cumulative downtime?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A poison pill message causes consumer thread to crash repeatedly. How do you isolate this message to a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) without losing partition ordering?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Network egress costs between Kafka brokers and consumers across AWS Availability Zones cost $10,000/month. How do you optimize partition rack awareness?

counter_probes.counter_question: If you increase `max.poll.interval.ms` to 30 minutes, what happens when a consumer node genuinely dies due to hardware power loss? How long does that partition sit unconsumed?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Increasing timeout delays failure detection of real dead nodes. The correct solution is static membership (group.instance.id) and offloading processing to bounded worker pools while keeping poll() loop active.
